UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

For an ISIC 7490 game-art BPO, pure mail-forwarding virtual offices may be challenged as sham under tax-residence and commercial-substance rules; a co-working or telework hub with documented operations is preferred.

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil y de Bienes Muebles de Madrid for company registration.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), arts. 3-4, 11, 20-22, 121-124, 175-180; Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), arts. 2-3 on digital incorporation and reduced minimum capital.

Formation / constitutional filings

Notarial public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) filed with the Mercantile Registry together with the application for registration.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 25 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

SL has no statutory minimum above €1; if share capital is set below €3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to a legal reserve until capital plus legal reserve equals €3,000. All cash contributions must be fully paid and deposited at the time the deed is granted; no escrow or notarial escrow account is required.

Funding & unlock path: Fire-safety certification for office/studio occupancy with fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation signage; building structural load inspection confirming safe office use; workplace health and safety clearance under Law 31/1995 and Royal Decree 486/1997, including ergonomic workstations, ventilation, and electrical installation checks.

Paid-in capital rule: SL has no statutory minimum above €1; if share capital is set below €3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to a legal reserve until capital plus legal reserve equals €3,000. All cash contributions must be fully paid and deposited at the time the deed is granted; no escrow or notarial escrow account is required.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
At a duly convened general meeting of the sole incorporator/shareholder held in Madrid on [date], it was resolved: (1) To subscribe and fully pay the share capital of €1,000 divided into 1,000 indivisible quotas, as set out in the deed; (2) To adopt the Articles of Association, approve the corporate purpose covering 3D art and character rigging services, and adopt the registered office at Calle Gran Vía 28, Madrid; (3) To appoint the sole administrator and shareholder as legal representative with powers for banking, contracting, and licensing; (4) To authorize filing with the Mercantile Registry, obtaining the Tax Identification Number, and commencing operations upon inscription.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo – Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas de la Comunidad de Madrid

Category: No mandatory operating or manufacturing license; the office-based 3D art outsourcing activity is subject only to the municipal declaration of responsible activity.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); corporate income tax returns via Modelo 200/220; VAT via Modelos 303/349/390; customs delegated to Dependencia de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales.

E-government filing portal

Upon incorporation of the SL before a Spanish notary, the promoter obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by filing Modelo 036 at the competent provincial AEAT office. After inscription in the Registro Mercantil, the provisional NIF becomes definitive; the entity then files Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF certificate. Simultaneously, the SL registers for VAT (IVA) on the same Modelo 036, thereby obtaining the NIF-IVA (format ES-B[8 digits][control]). Foreign shareholders or group entities without a Spanish permanent establishment must obtain a non-resident NIF with prefix 'N' via Modelo 036 and, if not established in the EU/EEA, appoint a resident tax representative (representante fiscal) when required by law.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Spanish-resident SL is an opaque taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (CIT) under Ley 27/2014 (TRLIS) at a standard 25% rate; new entities enjoy a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base for their first two profitable years; the SL is never fiscally transparent in Spain. — Upon incorporation of the SL before a Spanish notary, the promoter obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by filing Modelo 036 at the competent provincial AEAT office. After inscription in the Registro Mercantil, the provisional NIF becomes definitive; the entity then files Modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF certificate. Simultaneously, the SL registers for VAT (IVA) on the same Modelo 036, thereby obtaining the NIF-IVA (format ES-B[8 digits][control]). Foreign shareholders or group entities without a Spanish permanent establishment must obtain a non-resident NIF with prefix 'N' via Modelo 036 and, if not established in the EU/EEA, appoint a resident tax representative (representante fiscal) when required by law.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation; a Spanish-resident SL is an opaque taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (CIT) under Ley 27/2014 (TRLIS) at a standard 25% rate; new entities enjoy a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base for their first two profitable years; the SL is never fiscally transparent in Spain.

Available election forms

No US-style check-the-box election exists; the SL is mandatorily opaque. Available elections include: (i) CIT group consolidation (Arts. 64-111 TRLIS) where a Spanish parent holds at least 75% (70% for listed entities) of a subsidiary; (ii) reduced CIT rate for newly incorporated entities (Art. 29.2 TRLIS); (iii) patent box regime (Art. 23 TRLIS) for qualifying IP income; (iv) VAT refund fast-track via REDEME monthly regime; (v) cash-basis VAT for SMEs with turnover below EUR 2,000,000; (vi) intra-community VAT grouping under Arts. 163 bis decies et seq. Ley IVA; and (vii) election to claim EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive zero withholding on dividends. ATAD II hybrid rules (Art. 15ter TRLIS) may re-characterise the SL as a reverse hybrid if all non-resident direct or indirect shareholders are located in jurisdictions that treat the SL as transparent.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0 — no de minimis turnover threshold; every taxable person carrying out taxable supplies in Spain must register via Modelo 036 before commencing operations. For intra-community acquisitions by non-deductible persons, the annual exemption threshold is EUR 10,000; a fully taxable SL is outside this exception and must at all times hold a valid NIF-IVA for intra-EU trade.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

An SL may apply 0% VAT (exemption with right to deduction) to: (i) exports of goods physically leaving the EU customs territory (Art. 21 Ley IVA), provided exit is evidenced within 90 days; (ii) intra-EU B2B supplies of services under Art. 69(1) Ley IVA where the customer is established in another Member State and holds a valid VAT number, with the invoice citing 'inversión del sujeto pasivo'; and (iii) services to customers established outside the EU (Art. 69 Ley IVA), including digital game art, 3D sculpting, rigging and asset licensing, where such services are not effectively connected to Spanish immovable property or on-site work in Spain. Substantiation requires an enforceable service contract, complete digital delivery logs, valid foreign tax identification of the customer, and proof of payment; the corresponding input VAT remains fully deductible subject to the pro-rata rules.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) with the assigned EORI reference and customs exit stamp or NCTS/EXS electronic exit confirmation
  • Transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill (AWB), CMR consignment note or rail/sea manifest
  • Commercial invoice with HS classification of exported media (e.g., HS 8523 for digital game assets embodied on physical media) and Incoterms 2020
  • Packing list and value declaration supporting the declared export amount
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de divisas) or SWIFT MT103 / correspondent bank credit advice evidencing settlement of the export proceeds
  • Intangible service export dossier for pure digital deliverables: signed outsourcing agreement, IP assignment or licence documentation, delivery logs with timestamps and evidence of client acceptance

SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) is mandatory for taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04, VAT groups and REDEME registrants; invoice records must be transmitted to AEAT through SII web services (SOAP/XML with X.509 certificate, Facturae 3.2 format) within 4 business days (8 calendar days for bulk simplified submissions). For all other SLs, Ley 18/2022 Crea y Crece mandates B2B electronic invoicing once the implementing royal decree is in force (expected during 2025). Verifactu (RD 1007/2023) requires qualified billing software generating hash-chained invoice records identified by 'VERI*FACTU' from 1 July 2025; no real-time fiscal stamp is required pre-clearance, but invoice records must be accessible to AEAT during inspection and may include a QR verification code.

AEAT systematically cross-matches export declarations and zero-rated invoices against the customs SIGE database, VIES intra-EU records and bank foreign-exchange data; any mismatch or documentary gap triggers retroactive recharacterisation of the supply as taxable at 21% plus statutory late-payment interest. Administrative penalties under Arts. 191 and 198 LGT range from 50% to 150% of the under-declared amount, with fixed penalties under Art. 201 LGT of EUR 150 to EUR 300 or 1% per month of VAT where invoice documentation is defective. If the VAT or tax loss exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal may result in imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount; amounts above EUR 600,000 or committed within an organised group trigger Art. 305bis with sentences of 2 to 6 years. Undue refunds obtained are clawed back within the four-year statute of limitation, and the SL may be suspended from REDEME and lose AEO certification.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain applies full and unrestricted currency convertibility as a eurozone member state. Both current-account payments (dividends, royalties, service fees, interest, profit remittances) and capital-account operations (equity injections, shareholder loans, loan repayments and repatriation of liquidation proceeds) are liberalised under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the national implementing framework of Law 19/2003. No exchange-control licence, no prior convertibility approval, and no waiting period is imposed on an SL distributing its after-tax earnings to non-resident shareholders; the only frictions are the ordinary 19% dividend withholding tax applicable to non-resident shareholders and the availability of treaty relief (reduced to between 0% and 10% under EU Directives or the Spain-Latin America double-tax treaties such as Mexico, Argentina, Chile and Colombia). The euro is fully convertible into USD, GBP, JPY or any other globally tradeable currency at market rates through the commercial banks, without central-bank rationing. The remaining compliance burden is informatory rather than authorisation-based: transactions crossing regulatory thresholds must be reported through the Bank of Spain's statistical balance-of-payments form and, where the operation is a foreign direct investment of ten percent or more of the share capital or of control, through the post-transaction statement filed with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores. For a creative studio invoicing overseas game publishers, no material convertibility or remittance hurdle exists, provided the invoice chain, transfer-pricing file and beneficial-owner register are kept in good order.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligations and no mandatory conversion ratios on receipts from exported services. A resident SL supplying 3D sculpting, character rigging and art outsourcing to foreign game publishers may freely keep receivables in USD, GBP, JPY or EUR in domestic foreign-currency accounts, or may leave them offshore with the same tax transparency, subject to correct accounting and declaration in the annual corporate income tax return (Modelo 200). There is no statutory repatriation deadline, no obligation to liquidate foreign balances, and no penalty for retaining export earnings outside the euro area; the Bank of Spain's balance-of-payments declaration applies only to the statistical collection of settlement flows above stated thresholds. The operative compliance duties are: (i) issue of an accurate invoice identifying the non-resident client and the place of supply, (ii) Spanish VAT application under the place-of-supply rule that generally removes B2B digital service income from the Spanish VAT base where the client is a taxable person in another jurisdiction, subject to the Modelo 349 recapitulative statement where required, and (iii) documentation of economic substance sufficient to defeat any allegation of diverted income or passive foreign-investment-company treatment. No surrender certificate, no exchange approval and no conversion receipt is required from the Bank of Spain before the funds are used for treasury or distribution purposes.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating as the national competent authority within the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem, exercises prudential supervision over Spanish credit institutions, foreign-currency statistical reporting, and balance-of-payments declarations under the capital-movement regime. Administrative and policy authority over cross-border capital flows is shared with the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, which maintains the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Foreign Investment Registry) under Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree-Law 5/2023, as amended by Law 8/2023. Operational AML/CFT oversight of banks and electronic-money institutions is exercised by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias), the Spanish Financial Intelligence Unit. The Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) supervises listed issuers, investment services, and FX derivatives providers; for a standard Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada engaged in cross-border 3D art outsourcing, the day-to-day authority is the Bank of Spain through the clearing bank and the foreign-investment registry through the Ministry.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% final withholding tax on dividends and profit distributions paid to non-resident shareholders, unless a domestic exemption, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or double tax treaty reduces the rate (commonly 0-10%).

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within six months and twenty-five calendar days after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, the filing window runs from 1 July to 25 July of the following year

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 00001 (Page 1 - tax identification) Tax identification number (NIF) of the Spanish limited liability company, corporate name, registered office, and financial year-end Non-resident shareholders do not file this form; the Spanish SL must report its own NIF and corporate data. Shareholder residency is disclosed separately via beneficial ownership declarations. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.
Box 00200 (Page 2 - accounting result) Net accounting profit or loss before tax adjustments, derived from the statutory profit and loss account prepared under Spanish GAAP The foreign parent or service recipient must not commingle its own accounts here; all amounts must relate solely to the Spanish operational entity. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.
Boxes 00310-00360 (correction of accounting result and permanent/temporary adjustments) Extract from the reconciliation between accounting result and taxable income, including depreciation, amortisation, provisions, and non-deductible expenses Cross-border service fees paid to the Spanish entity must be arm's length; penalty or default interest charges and fictitious expenses must be adjusted as permanent differences. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.
Box 00550 (taxable base) Taxable income for the Spanish corporate income tax after application of carryforwards, set-offs, and regime adjustments This figure is the foundation for the final tax liability. A non-resident shareholder cannot use losses or credits of the Spanish company in its own jurisdiction. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.
Box 00608 (gross tax liability) Tax computed by applying the applicable rate (generally 25%) to the taxable base, before deductions and credits Any withholding tax credit or treaty relief relevant to foreign shareholders is not handled in this box; it is applied separately when the dividend is distributed. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.
Box 00650 (payments on account and withholdings) Prepayments of corporate income tax, instalment payments made during the year, and any withholdings suffered by the company Non-resident shareholders cannot reclaim these amounts; instalment payments are the exclusive obligation of the Spanish entity. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.
Box 00695 (result of the tax return) Final net amount payable or refundable, including any self-assessment adjustments Payment must be settled in euro from a Spanish bank account or by direct debit. Failure to pay triggers enforced collection and surcharges. Late filing without prior AEAT notice: progressive i) 5% unpaid if filed within 3 months late; ii) 10% within 3-6 months; iii) 15% within 6-12 months; iv) 20% after 12 months, plus default interest. If filed after AEAT notice, the penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the lost tax. Non-filing without tax loss attracts fixed penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 10,000 depending on turnover; filing after official request triggers additional sanctions.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Local File required for taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 10,000,000 that carry out related-party transactions; Master File required for entities belonging to a multi-national group with consolidated turnover above EUR 20,000,000 (or lower EU-derived thresholds). Any cross-border related-party transaction individually exceeding EUR 100,000 must be disclosed annually in Modelo 232 and be supported by contemporaneous functional and risk analysis.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, the Spanish General Anti-Abuse Rule (Ley 58/2003, article 15), the European ATAD anti-abuse rules, and the CFC regime require real economic substance: physical office or establishment in Spain, actual employees and decision-making, and a genuine business purpose. Lack of substance is a decisive factor in re-characterising the Spanish SL as a resident shell, denying treaty benefits, and imposing penalties under the anti-avoidance framework.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion (Infracción tributaria grave / Delito contra la Hacienda Pública)

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the under-declared tax plus default interest; if criminal evasion is established, imprisonment of 2 to 6 years, a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of public subsidies or benefits.

Director personal liability: Directors, de facto managers, or legal representatives may be personally liable for the unpaid tax under LGT article 42. In criminal cases, the same persons are criminally responsible for the evasion; the corporate veil is pierced for assets acquired with the defrauded amount, and travel bans or provisional imprisonment can be ordered.
Shell Company / Abuse of Legal Form (Abuso de forma y simulación)

Statutory sanction: AEAT re-characterises the transaction under the GAAR: taxable income is recalculated, treaty relief is denied, and a penalty surcharge of 20% to 40% applies to the corrected tax. Intragroup payments to blacklisted or non-cooperative jurisdictions may face a special 19% withholding tax at gross, with no credit.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly participated in or installed the shell structure are jointly liable for the resulting tax debt. Criminal tax or money laundering proceedings can be joined; the court may disable the director from managing other companies and seize personal assets.
Money Laundering and AML Deficiencies

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines under AML Law 10/2010: minor infringements EUR 300 to EUR 150,000; serious infringements EUR 150,000 to EUR 600,000; very serious infringements up to EUR 5,000,000 or 5% of the offender's turnover. Criminal money laundering independently carries imprisonment up to 6 years and confiscation of assets.

Director personal liability: Directors are personally liable for AML penalties where they knowingly carried out or ordered the operation. Criminal conviction for money laundering leads to personal imprisonment, disqualification from professional practice, and separate monetary fines. In serious cases, the corporate veil is disregarded and directors may face travel bans and preventive seizure.
Failure to Prepare Transfer Pricing Documentation

Statutory sanction: Penalty of EUR 1,500 to EUR 50,000 per missing or incomplete documentation set; in addition, AEAT may perform a unilateral adjustment and apply a 15% to 20% surcharge on the corrected tax. The company cannot rely on the arm's length standard without compliant documentation.

Director personal liability: The director who certifies or approves the tax return is directly responsible for the inaccuracy; if the TP adjustments lead to under-declared tax, the personal joint liability regime under LGT article 42.1(a) applies, with civil liability and procedural interception orders.
